💬 Reference

Copilot Prompt Library

Copy-paste prompts for common PMM tasks. Tested and refined.

These prompts work. Copy them, customize the bracketed sections, and iterate from there.

📝 Content & Messaging

Positioning Statement

Generate a positioning statement in the classic format.

For [target customer] who [statement of need], [product name] is a [product category] that [key benefit]. Unlike [competitor/alternative], we [primary differentiator]. Fill this in for [your product]. Make the benefit specific and measurable where possible.

Value Proposition with Proof Points

Create value props that can withstand "so what?" scrutiny.

Create 3 value propositions for [product] targeting [persona]. For each value prop: - State the benefit in outcome terms (not feature terms) - Include a quantified proof point or customer example - Add the "so what" — why this matters to their job/goals Avoid generic claims. Be specific to this buyer's context.

Blog Post Outline

Structure a thought leadership piece.

Create an outline for a blog post titled "[title]". Audience: [persona] Goal: [educate/persuade/announce] Length: [word count target] Include: - Hook (first paragraph that earns the read) - 4-6 subheadings with key points for each - Data or examples to include - CTA at the end Make it opinionated, not a list of obvious points.

Email Sequence

Draft a nurture or announcement sequence.

Write a 3-email sequence for [campaign goal]. Audience: [persona] Context: [what prompted this outreach] Email 1: [objective - e.g., introduce problem] Email 2: [objective - e.g., present solution] Email 3: [objective - e.g., drive action] Keep each email under 150 words. Conversational tone. Clear single CTA per email.

🎯 Competitive & Market

Competitive Battlecard

One-page competitive comparison for sales.

Create a competitive battlecard: [our product] vs [competitor]. Include: 1. Positioning comparison (one paragraph each) 2. Feature comparison table (6-8 key capabilities) 3. Where we win / Where they win 4. Top 3 objections and responses 5. Discovery questions to ask 6. Landmine questions to plant Target user: Sales rep in a competitive deal.

Win/Loss Analysis Questions

Generate interview questions for win/loss research.

I'm conducting win/loss interviews for [product] deals. Generate 15 interview questions covering: - Decision criteria and process - Perception of our solution vs alternatives - What tipped the decision - Surprises or concerns during evaluation - Advice for us going forward Mix closed and open-ended. Order from rapport-building to probing.

Market Sizing

Structure a TAM/SAM/SOM analysis.

Help me size the market for [product/solution]. Context: - Product category: [description] - Target segment: [industry, company size, geo] - Price point: [approximate] Structure a TAM/SAM/SOM analysis with: - Methodology for each level - Data sources I should reference - Key assumptions to state - Sanity checks to apply

📊 Analysis & Strategy

Executive Summary

Compress a long document for leadership.

Summarize this for an executive audience: [paste document] Create: 1. Bottom line (one sentence, action-oriented) 2. Three key findings (bullet points) 3. Recommendation or next step 4. Risks or caveats Under 200 words total. No jargon.

Strategy Stress Test

Pressure-test a plan before presenting.

Act as a skeptical executive reviewing this strategy: [paste strategy/plan] 1. What are the 3 biggest weaknesses? 2. What questions will a CFO ask? 3. What's missing from this plan? 4. Rate argument strength 1-10 and explain 5. What's the strongest counter-argument? Be direct. I need critique, not validation.

Meeting Prep

Prepare for a customer or stakeholder meeting.

I have a meeting with [company/person] tomorrow. Context: - Company: [name, industry, size] - Meeting purpose: [discovery/demo/review] - Attendees: [roles] - What I know: [any background] Help me prepare: 1. Likely priorities and pain points 2. Questions I should ask 3. Topics to avoid or be careful with 4. How to open the conversation 5. Ideal outcome and how to get there

🔄 Repurposing & Adaptation

Content Repurposer

Turn one piece into multiple formats.

Repurpose this content for multiple channels: [paste content] Create: 1. LinkedIn post (under 200 words, strong hook) 2. Email teaser (3 sentences + CTA) 3. Twitter/X thread (5 tweets) 4. Slack announcement (casual, internal) 5. Executive talking points (3 bullets) Same core message, adapted tone/format per channel.

Persona Adapter

Reframe content for a different audience.

Adapt this content for a different persona: Original content (written for [original persona]): [paste content] New target: [new persona - e.g., technical buyer vs business buyer] Rewrite to: - Address their specific concerns - Use language they use - Emphasize benefits relevant to their role - Adjust technical depth appropriately

✍️ Writing & Editing

Tone Shifter

Adjust writing tone without changing meaning.

Rewrite this in a [formal/casual/urgent/confident] tone: [paste text] Keep the same meaning and key points. Just change how it sounds.

Jargon Killer

Simplify complex or buzzword-heavy writing.

Simplify this text. Remove jargon, buzzwords, and unnecessary complexity: [paste text] Rules: - Replace abstract terms with concrete examples - Cut words that don't add meaning - Use active voice - If a simpler word exists, use it A smart 8th grader should understand it.

Editor Mode

Get constructive feedback on your writing.

Edit this writing and explain your changes: [paste text] Focus on: - Clarity and flow - Removing redundancy - Strengthening weak claims - Improving the opening and closing Show the edited version, then list 3-5 specific changes you made and why.
